planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; Aker's West Virginia is a potato-leaf Appalachian family heirloom preserved through Seed Savers Exchange, grown for its huge pink beefsteak fruit.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, then transplant into deeply worked, fertile ground once nights stay reliably above 50F. Aker's West Virginia is a potato-leaf Appalachian family heirloom that produces very large, rosy-pink beefsteak fruit with meaty, low-acid flesh in the style of other West Virginia pink tomatoes, but on a distinct, separately preserved family line. Cage or stake plants early since the heavy fruit clusters can bend unsupported stems, and water evenly through fruit set to reduce cracking. Best suited to gardeners who already have room for one or two vigorous, long-season indeterminate vines.

planting.note: Start indoors 5-6 weeks before the last frost; this old currant-type heirloom sets heavy clusters of tiny yellow fruit and benefits from early staking on its sprawling vines.

directions: Sow indoors 5-6 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once the soil has warmed, giving vines a trellis or tall cage since they sprawl readily. Hartman's Yellow Gooseberry is a historic small-fruited heirloom that sets long, grape-like clusters of marble-sized, golden-yellow fruit with a tart-sweet, old-fashioned currant-tomato flavor. The prolific, viny plants keep producing over a long season and are well suited to pickling or preserves as well as fresh snacking. Pick clusters whole once fruit has fully colored, since individual berries continue to size up unevenly within a truss.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; Sandul Moldovan is an Eastern European pink beefsteak heirloom that fruits reliably even in shorter, cooler summers.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into well-drained, fertile soil after frost danger passes, staking or caging the vigorous indeterminate vines. Sandul Moldovan is a pink beefsteak heirloom from Moldova valued for setting a heavy crop of smooth, meaty, 8-12 ounce fruit even where summers run shorter or cooler than the Deep South. The flavor is mild, sweet, and well balanced, with dense flesh and relatively few seeds that make it a good choice for slicing and canning alike. Maintain even soil moisture during fruit development to minimize cracking on the smooth-skinned fruit.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; this German heirloom forms hollow, air-pocketed fruit prized for stuffing rather than dense slicing flesh.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil once nights warm, caging the indeterminate vines for support. Schimmeig Striped Hollow is a German heirloom whose red-and-orange striped fruit develops distinctive hollow chambers around the seed cavities instead of dense slicing flesh, a trait that makes it a novelty choice for stuffing with rice, meat, or grain fillings. Flavor is mild and the texture is notably different from typical slicing tomatoes, so it is grown more for its unusual form and culinary use than for fresh eating. Harvest when fully striped and firm, since overripe fruit can collapse at the hollow centers.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; Tappy's Heritage is a pink beefsteak heirloom preserved through the Seed Savers Exchange network.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into deeply prepared, fertile soil after all danger of frost has passed, supporting vines with a sturdy cage or stake from the start. Tappy's Heritage is a pink beefsteak heirloom that produces large, meaty, slightly flattened fruit with a classic sweet-tart old-fashioned flavor on vigorous indeterminate vines. It rewards consistent watering and feeding through the season with a long harvest window rather than one concentrated flush. Pick fruit when fully colored but still firm for the best balance of flavor and shelf life.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; Olena Ukrainian sets large, heart-shaped orange fruit on vigorous indeterminate vines.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil once frost danger has passed, staking plants to support the large oxheart fruit. Olena Ukrainian is an orange-fruited heirloom from Ukraine that forms distinctly pointed, heart-shaped fruit often exceeding a pound, with dense, meaty, low-acid flesh and relatively few seeds. The mild, sweet flavor and smooth texture make it popular for slicing and sauce alike, and the indeterminate vines crop steadily through a long warm season. Water evenly during fruit development to limit cracking on the large, heavy fruit.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; Thessaloniki is a Greek pink beefsteak heirloom valued for good crack resistance and heavy yields.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm, fertile soil after frost risk has passed, caging or staking the indeterminate vines early. Thessaloniki is a Greek heirloom named for the region around its namesake city, producing abundant clusters of medium-to-large pink fruit with a well-balanced sweet-tart flavor and notably good resistance to cracking in humid weather. The vines are productive over a long season and tend to hold up well under heat stress typical of Mediterranean-climate summers. Harvest regularly once fruit colors fully to keep plants setting new flushes.

planting.note: Start indoors 5-6 weeks before the last frost; Pink Ping Pong is a small round pink cherry tomato that fruits early and sets heavy clusters.

directions: Sow indoors 5-6 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once the soil has warmed, providing a cage or trellis for the sprawling indeterminate vines. Pink Ping Pong produces round, smooth, pink cherry tomatoes about the size and shape of a table-tennis ball, borne in heavy clusters with a sweet, well-balanced flavor. The compact-fruited habit makes it a reliable early producer for fresh snacking and salads through a long summer season. Pick fruit promptly as it ripens to encourage continued flowering and set.
